steps.description: Load the counts and metadata, check that sample columns and metadata rows align exactly (reorder metadata to the count column order; fail loudly on any mismatch). Round the fractional RSEM expected counts to integers (round, not floor/ceiling) and record how many entries changed and the largest fractional part, since the negative binomial model requires integers. Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~ condition. Report per-sample library size (column sum) and number of detected genes (count > 0) in a table, flagging sample_01 explicitly against the median. Apply the blind variance stabilizing transformation, run PCA on the 500 most variable genes coloured by condition and labelled by sample, and draw a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap. State in writing whether sample_01 departs from its group beyond what depth explains and whether there is a stated reason to remove it — do not remove it by default. plan.title: Colon RSEM counts: treated vs control DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level count matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 samples plus the gene id column) with a sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv, 12 rows, one condition column) for human colon tissue: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch. The question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan is a two-group differential expression analysis and nothing more — no enrichment step was asked for.

Two facts from the profile drive the design. First, the matrix holds RSEM expected counts, which are fractional, and the per-sample genes.results files carrying effective lengths were not delivered. A quantifier name alone does not establish that a length correction occurred, and tximport cannot be run on an already-summarized gene table. The plan therefore rounds the expected counts to integers for the negative binomial model and fits on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and it states explicitly in the report that the average-transcript-length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can therefore appear as differential expression. The correct remedy — the per-sample genes.results files or a per-gene per-sample average transcript length table — is named as a request in the report rather than fabricated.

Second, sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. It is kept through QC and inspected on the PCA, the sample distance heatmap, and the library-size/detected-gene table, not silently dropped: median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth, and a low-depth sample simply carries less information (wider interval). Removal would need a stated reason from the QC, and the QC step is instructed to state one if it finds one; the primary DE fit uses all 12 samples, with a sensitivity refit excluding sample_01 reported as a secondary check on whether any called gene depends on it.

The fit is DESeq2 with design ~condition, control set explicitly as the reference level so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for ranking, independent filtering on, and Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and returns NA p-values, so NAs from the outlier flag are reported separately from NAs from the independent filter. Because n=6 per group sits in the range where DESeq2 and edgeR disagree at the margins, an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is run on the same counts and design as a robustness check, and the intersection is reported as the high-confidence set — never the union.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~ condition with explicit reference level control, counts as delivered without length offset
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, method overlap

Genes unique to one method are not failures of the other — report them as method-specific, secondary

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
